title: Select and disable stable scheduled bindings
summary: Interpret or change exact definition selection, generated user LaunchAgents, transition journals, compensation, disabling, and launchd delivery limits.
use_when: A stable product key should select a registered definition or remain inactive.
Generated schedule ownership, coherent cutover, interrupted transitions, or disabled selection must be understood.
do_not_use_when: The actual goal is registration, direct process execution, incident approval, or program installation.
The caller intends to edit plist/SQLite directly, bypass ownership, or create parallel generations.
outcome: One coherent selected or inactive stable binding, or a retained refusal with recovery evidence.
effects: Switch and disable change recorded selection, generated plist and launchd loaded state under per-key locks and transition journals.
Switch or compensation with run-at-load can request product work after the gate opens; disable stops new admission and normally waits for natural completion.
authority: Clockwork owns binding selection and generated projection; products own maintenance, domain work and rollback basis; launchd owns timer delivery.
success: Returned success proves selected database state, digest-attributed plist bytes and loaded state agree.
failure_and_recovery: Compensate to exact prior state, or attempt durable disable while attributable. Retain unknown projections and journals without mutation.
A child whose broker disappeared must be proved absent before disable can proceed. Unknown commit durability is reported without unjournaled rollback.
privacy: Definition selections, paths, schedule and runtime correlation remain private current-user metadata.
does_not_authorize: Product retry, incident approval, release deployment, deletion of history/state/artifacts, or intentional dual old-and-new schedules.

consumers.statement: A current-user operator or product lifecycle tool may inspect, select, disable or recover an exact same-key binding.

preconditions.statement: Switch requires an existing same-key definition, inactive activation, maintained product gate, validated prior state, exact content-addressed installed broker, filesystem authority and available current-user launchd GUI domain.

inputs.statement: Inputs are a stable key and, for switch or disabled selection recovery, an existing definition digest. Runtime process context is never accepted here.

outputs.statement: Public commands print plain text by default. --json selects the existing compact ok:true/data JSON envelope and coded ok:false/error JSON on stderr with exit one. Machine callers must pass --json.

Binding receipts expose recorded selected digest, enabled intent, halted_incident and failure_policy_active. Lists use output version two, items/has_more, default 20 and positive --limit. Show does not query launchd or expose private plist digest.

data_semantics.statement: A binding selects one nullable immutable same-key definition. Disabled existing keys retain selection; absent disable creates a null-selection tombstone. The plist digest proves ownership of exact generated bytes.

identity_and_units.statement: Stable owner/name maps to org.clockwork.owner.name. Definition and plist identities are separate SHA-256 digests. Whole Unix seconds describe retained update time.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: List/show read recorded local binding state at invocation; launchd alignment is checked during transitions, not inferred from inspection.
No future delivery, maximum start delay, catch-up count, fairness or availability percentage is promised.

access.statement: Current-user local CLI and typed client operate private bindings and owned user LaunchAgents.
Direct plist or SQLite editing, system/root services, and same-user authentication by namespace are unsupported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Per-key management and transition gates serialize database/plist/loaded-state changes. Existing projections receive a durable exact prior/candidate journal before mutation. Switch recovers prior state; disable replaces intent and consumes journals directly into inactivity. Unknown projections are retained. Journal-unlink sync uncertainty retains coherent state.

Disable prevents new admission and waits through a live broker; orphaned live/unknown children cause restore/refusal. Disabled --select never loads a timer. Selection, disable, compensation and rollback preserve independent incidents.

operational_limits.statement: One current-user generated schedule uses the exact installed Clockwork binary and stable key, not product executable/argv/secrets.
No compare-and-swap condition covers a product deployer's earlier ownership inspection; product tools must serialize their own use. Concurrent direct same-user mutation is unsupported.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Binding identity, selected definition, failure incident and installed program selector remain independent; changed launch meaning needs explicit selection.
No general migration window, retention horizon or deprecation interval is promised.

reliances.statement: Generated schedule loading and timer delivery rely on per-user macOS launchd, GUI login, sleep/wake, clocks/time zones, filesystem access and TCC; no dedicated installed contract describes launchd.
